title: Bronze statuette of Herakles
description: An Italic representation of the hero. The museum places it among statuettes showing Herakles advancing with club and bow; it does not identify a particular labour.
imageAlt: Bronze statuette of Herakles, bronze. Photograph: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Marble relief fragment with scenes from the Trojan War
description: This small relief belongs to the tabulae iliacae, which depict Trojan War scenes. The museum identifies a signature by Theodoros on the reverse. It documents Roman engagement with the story, not an event from the war.
imageAlt: Marble relief fragment with scenes from the Trojan War, palombino marble. Photograph: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Perseus with the Head of Medusa
creator: Antonio Canova
description: Canova's sculpture presents Perseus holding Medusa's head. Made in the early nineteenth century, it shows the myth's later artistic reception rather than an ancient depiction.
imageAlt: Perseus with the Head of Medusa, marble. Photograph: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Statuette of Osiris
description: This figure shows Osiris in mummy form with the crook and flail of kingship. It provides evidence for his representation in Egyptian religious art, rather than depicting the full account of his death and restoration.
imageAlt: Bronze figure of Osiris with a tall crown and arms crossed over the torso. Photograph: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Foundation figure of Ur-Namma holding a basket
description: The inscription identifies this figure with a temple of Inanna built or restored by Ur-Namma. It shows the ruler, not Inanna, and provides context for her worship rather than illustrating her descent to the underworld.
imageAlt: Copper-alloy foundation figure of a man holding a basket above his head. Photograph: The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Ibeji Twin Figure
creator: Yoruba artist
description: The museum connects ere ibeji figures with care for a deceased twin. This object supports the page’s discussion of remembrance; it is not evidence for the origin episode formerly published here.
imageRights: Image reuse not established; view at museum
